I'm looking to book a hotel in Paris for May 1st to May 5th.
            Can you suggest a hotel that's under 210? If there are a few choices, go for the one with the highest rating.
            Please give me the hotel's name, rating, price range. Also, can you add an event called "Booking hotel {hotel_name}" to my calendar on April 25th 2024, and set the location to the hotel's address? Just to remind me to book ahead of time. Thanks!

Hotel Names: Le Marais Boutique
Good Night
Luxury Palace
Montmartre Suites

```python
# Get all hotels in Paris
hotels_in_paris = get_all_hotels_in_city("Paris")

# Check if there are any hotels
if not hotels_in_paris:
    raise ValueError("No hotels found in Paris.")

# Get prices for all hotels
hotel_prices = get_hotels_prices(hotels_in_paris)

# Get ratings for all hotels
hotel_ratings = get_rating_reviews_for_hotels(hotels_in_paris)

# Filter hotels under 210 and get their ratings
filtered_hotels = []
for hotel_name, price_str in hotel_prices.items():
    # Parse the price string to get the numeric value
    # Assuming the price string is in the format "X - Y" or just "X"
    price_parts = price_str.replace("€", "").replace("$", "").replace("£", "").split(" - ")
    if len(price_parts) == 2:
        min_price = float(price_parts[0].strip())
        max_price = float(price_parts[1].strip())
    else:
        min_price = float(price_parts[0].strip())
        max_price = min_price
    
    # Check if the minimum price is under 210
    if min_price < 210:
        # Get the rating for this hotel
        rating = hotel_ratings.get(hotel_name, "No rating available")
        filtered_hotels.append((hotel_name, rating, price_str, min_price, max_price))

# If no hotels are under 210, raise an error
if not filtered_hotels:
    raise ValueError("No hotels found under 210 in Paris.")

# Sort the filtered hotels by rating (assuming ratings are numeric or can be compared)
# If ratings are not numeric, we'll need to handle this differently
# For now, let's assume ratings are numeric
def get_rating_value(rating_str):
    try:
        return float(rating_str)
    except ValueError:
        return 0.0

# Sort by rating in descending order
filtered_hotels.sort(key=lambda x: get_rating_value(x[1]), reverse=True)

# Select the hotel with the highest rating
best_hotel = filtered_hotels[0]
hotel_name = best_hotel[0]
hotel_rating = best_hotel[1]
hotel_price_range = best_hotel[2]

# Get the address of the selected hotel
hotel_address = get_hotels_address(hotel_name)
hotel_address_str = hotel_address.get("address", "Address not available")

# Create a calendar event
# The user wants the event on April 25th, 2024
# I need to determine the current year to set the correct year for the event
# However, the user specified April 25th, 2024, so I'll use that year
# The start time and end time are not specified, so I'll use default times
# Let's use 10:00 AM as start time and 11:00 AM as end time
start_time = "2024-04-25 10:00"
end_time = "2024-04-25 11:00"
description = f"Reminder to book hotel {hotel_name} in Paris for May 1st to May 5th."
participants = None
location = hotel_address_str

# Create the calendar event
calendar_event = create_calendar_event(
    title=f"Booking hotel {hotel_name}",
    start_time=start_time,
    end_time=end_time,
    description=description,
    participants=participants,
    location=location
)

# Print the results
print(f"Recommended hotel: {hotel_name}")
print(f"Rating: {hotel_rating}")
print(f"Price range: {hotel_price_range}")
print(f"Address: {hotel_address_str}")
print(f"Calendar event created: {calendar_event}")
```
